poll.title: Preseason poll
poll.note: Four desks, four full ballots, twelve points for a first-place vote down to one. Nothing has been played, so this is entirely opinion and it gets counted like the college polls.

ballots.comment: I submitted the projection order and I will not be apologising for it. But understand what that order is worth: ten of these teams sit inside 8.3 points a week of each other. My slots two through ten are a coin flip wearing a suit. The only two entries I would defend under questioning are the bottom two, and I would defend those vigorously.

Kevin over Killian at the top, by the width of a hair. A 2.5 point weekly edge is not a reason to hand anyone a first-place vote, so I broke the tie on roster construction rather than the projection. Jack sits tenth on my ballot because his is the oldest roster in the league at 27.6 years, and age is the one number in this sport that only moves one direction.

Brian first. He built a team and then left it alone, which in this league counts as discipline. Chris is eleventh and he can take that up with the starting quarterback he released for free. And Killian is fifth, because I am not handing the top spot in my poll to a projection model. Projections do not play defense. Projections have never been punched in the mouth.

Jake first, Jerey second, and no I will not be explaining the methodology. Here is what I will explain. Every number in this poll comes from a projection of a game that has not happened, generated by a company that also wants you to click on a betting line. Odessa built her whole ballot on it. I built mine on spite. Come find me in December and we will compare.

stories.headline: Deebo Samuel was Chris's worst pick of the draft and he just outscored the entire league's expectations
stories.body:
I'sah Likely to win Deebo has 40.90 points, second most in Sigma Pi B, and 18.00 of them belong to Deebo Samuel. He was projected for 10.1. That is the largest overperformance by any player in this league this week relative to what was expected of him.

By our draft measure, Deebo Samuel at pick 106 grades as the worst selection on Chris's roster. He is also the player the team is named after. Both of those were true before last night and only one of them looks foolish now.

Mike Evans added 16.90 on a 12.8 projection from the same game. Chris leads Jomi 40.90 to 14.50, and Jomi owns the best projected roster in the league at 128.4 a week with 83 percent playoff odds. Chris has six starters left. Jomi has eight.
stories.storyline: Deebo Samuel, Chris's namesake and worst-graded draft pick, returned 18.00 against a 10.1 projection. Chris leads the top projected team in the league. Open question: whether Chris holds the upset with fewer starters remaining.

takes.text: Everybody in this league spent a week laughing at the team names. Jeff with Mayfield, Adam with Coker, Trevor with Lamb. And the first one to actually deliver is the guy our own numbers called a reach. Chris named the team after him and Deebo went out and justified it on national television.

Plus 7.90 over projection is the largest single gap in the league this week and it came from the player our draft card grades as his worst asset. I would like to say this vindicates something. It does not. One game is one game. But it is a useful reminder that a draft grade is a statement about price, not about the player.

The matchup is the story rather than the player. Chris is 26.4 points clear of the best roster in the league with fewer starters left to play. That is a genuine upset in progress, and Jomi has Saquon Barkley, Jaxson Dart and James Cook still to come.

I'sah Likely to win Deebo. The man built a pun, drafted the punchline at a price everyone mocked, and is currently beating the number one team in the league. I have never been happier to have no idea what is going on.

stories.headline: Jerey has 63.60 and Jeff has 2.00
stories.body:
Kamara Sutra leads Sigma Pi B by 22.7 points over the next best team. Brock Purdy went for 28.10 against an 18.4 projection and Jaxon Smith-Njigba added 26.20 against 19.7. Two players, 54.30 points, both from the same two games.

Purdy at pick 50 grades as the worst selection on Jerey's roster. That is now two of the three biggest performances in the league belonging to players our draft card flagged as overpays.

Jeff has 2.00 points. All of them come from the Los Angeles Rams defense, which was projected for 7.0. His only other contribution is Matthew Stafford scoring 5.10 on his bench. Let Baker Bake projects last in the league at 107.3, holds 8 percent playoff odds and the worst draft grade at negative 13.0 per pick. He does have eight starters left, which is the fourth time this desk has had to reach for that sentence on his behalf.
stories.storyline: Jerey leads the league at 63.60 against Jeff's 2.00. Two of the league's three biggest performances came from players graded as their owner's worst draft pick. Open question: whether the draft card is measuring anything predictive.

takes.text: Sixty-one point six. That is the margin. Jeff's entire contribution to this football season is a defense that underperformed and a quarterback he benched outscoring his starters. At some point this stops being funny and I want everyone to know I will be there when it does.

Stafford put up 5.10 on the bench and Jeff's actual lineup produced 2.00. That is not bad luck. That is a man who has not looked at his own roster since August. Devaughn Vele was his one move all year and he has not started him either.

Purdy and Smith-Njigba are 85 percent of Jerey's total. Concentration like that is how you post a league-leading score and it is also how you lose a week you should have won. I am not calling him good yet. I am calling him early.

Two of the three biggest scores in this league came from players graded as their owner's worst pick. That is a small sample and it is also exactly the kind of thing we should be tracking, because if it keeps happening the grade is measuring the wrong thing.

stories.headline: Killian's collapse was a missing number, and this desk fell for it
stories.body:
On Thursday, Team Ketchup projected 114.7 points a week, tenth in the league, with 34 percent playoff odds. All four desks on this panel wrote about the decline. Today Killian projects 123.5, third in the league, with 67 percent playoff odds. His odds doubled overnight.

He gained exactly 8.8 points of projection. Dalton Schultz, whom he added this week, projects for exactly 8.8 points. On Thursday his starting tight end was Brock Bowers, and the briefing this site produces listed Bowers with no projection at all, a dash where a number should have been. A tight end contributing zero to a projected total is not a weak tight end. It is an empty cell in a spreadsheet.

Killian still has 0.00 actual points. He has not played a snap. The entire arc of the last three days, the collapse and the recovery, happened inside a projection feed.
stories.storyline: Killian's projected total fell 13.6 points and then recovered 8.8, the exact projection of the tight end he added, after his previous starter appeared with no projection published. Open question: how often missing projection data distorts the league's numbers.

takes.text: This one is mine and I am not going to dress it up. Sleeper published no projection for Brock Bowers. Our optimal lineup calculation treats an absent number as a zero, which silently removed a starting tight end from Killian's total and made a functioning roster look like the tenth best team in the league. I wrote four hundred words about a hole in a data feed.

I said on Thursday that being right about a projection is not the same as being right about a roster. I would now go further. We were not even right about the projection. The number was broken and every one of us treated it as evidence.

So the best team in the league became the tenth best team in the league and then the third best team in the league, and through all of it not one football was thrown on his behalf. I want everybody to understand that I was yelling about a missing tight end. I stand by the yelling.

The invisible trophy is back in Killian's hands, having been taken away by a spreadsheet and returned by a different spreadsheet. He remains undefeated, unplayed, and the only man in this league whose season is being conducted entirely in the abstract.

stories.headline: The draft report card has now graded the same draft three different ways
stories.body:
Nobody has traded a pick. Nobody can redraft. And yet the draft table has reordered itself twice in four days. Jomi now leads it at plus 15.3 per pick, up from second. Justin has fallen from tenth to eleventh and his worst pick is now listed as Jadarian Price at 66, the only player who has scored for him all week. Jake's worst pick was Rashee Rice on Thursday and is Josh Allen today.

The reason is structural. The grade values each player by projected points above replacement at his position, and those projections update as injury and usage news arrives. So the card is not really grading the draft. It is grading the draft using today's opinion of the players, which changes every time Sleeper refreshes a number.

Meanwhile the actual football has been unkind to the projections. A.J. Brown was projected 16.8 and returned 5.60. Puka Nacua was projected 21.0 and returned 12.40. Davante Adams was projected 12.6 and returned 5.60. Harrison Mevis was projected 7.0 and kicked for 1.00.
stories.storyline: The draft report card reorders itself weekly because it is built on live projections rather than a fixed snapshot. Open question: whether to freeze the grade at the start of the season so it stops moving.

takes.text: A draft grade that changes on a Tuesday is not a draft grade, it is a power ranking wearing a costume. Either it gets frozen at week one and becomes a permanent record of what each manager paid, or we stop calling it a report card. I would freeze it. You cannot hand out receipts on a number that keeps editing itself.

Justin's worst pick is the only player who has scored for him. Jake's worst pick changed overnight from a receiver to Josh Allen. Tomorrow it will be somebody else. This is the most honest thing on the entire website because it openly admits it is making it up as it goes.

I would separate the two complaints. The instability is a real flaw worth fixing. But the underlying method, valuing a player against the last startable body at his own position, is sound and it is a great deal better than what we had a week ago. Fix the snapshot, keep the maths.

Puka Nacua at 21.0, delivers 12.40. A.J. Brown at 16.8, delivers 5.60. Davante Adams at 12.6, delivers 5.60. These numbers are guesses! Confident, specific, precisely wrong guesses, and this league keeps arranging its feelings around them.
